inputs.text: An Indiana judge blocked a law that restricted abortion after the ACLU and Hoosier Jews for Choice argued it burdened religious freedom. The claim that this “turns liberty on its head” ignores who bears the cost when the state dictates what people may do with their bodies. Religious freedom cannot mean privileging one moral view while denying others the ability to make deeply personal decisions. Calling abortion a threat to society’s moral foundations only obscures the power imbalance: lawmakers should not impose their beliefs at the expense of people who need reproductive care.

output.main_topic: Indiana judge blocks abortion restriction after religious freedom challenge
output.narrative_frame: An editorial defense of reproductive autonomy that frames abortion restrictions as an imbalance of power and rejects privileging one moral view in the name of religious freedom.
opinions: The claim that blocking the law turns liberty on its head ignores who bears the cost of state restrictions on bodily decisions.
Religious freedom should not privilege one moral view or prevent others from making deeply personal decisions.
Calling abortion a threat to society’s moral foundations obscures a power imbalance.
Lawmakers should not impose their beliefs at the expense of people who need reproductive care.
